newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch sees mkts approving good pension scheme.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch sees mkts approving good pension scheme.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch, returning from a foreign tour on Thursday, said he had found "huge international interest" in proposals to create a compulsory pensions savings scheme but he expected that a well-designed scheme would not concern markets at all.
"They'll be very interested in the details of the design that emerges when the work is completed, and I think that is the key," he told Reuters at Wellington airport.
"A good, well-designed retirement savings scheme, I think, would be of no concern to them at all."

It was agreed when the conservative National Party and the nationalist New Zealand First Party formed a coalition in December that a compulsory superannuation savings scheme, favoured by NZ First, would be put to public vote.
A referendum is scheduled for September.
New Zealand First proposed a retirement savings scheme that would eventually see at least eight percent of income diverted into pension savings.
If approved, it would come into force in July, 1998.
The government is currently working to finalise the exact design of the proposed scheme that will be put to the vote. --Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
